We computed entire-sequence log probabilities for acceptable and unacceptable sentences in each pair using the minicons library. Accuracy scores reflect the proportion of pairs where the model assigned a higher probability to theacceptable sentence.
As an acceptability measure, SLOR normalizes sequence probabilities by controlling for sentence length and word frequency.

Participants rated each sentence on a 7-point Likert scale from 1 (completely unacceptable) to 7 (completely acceptable).

We assume that every participant uses the scale slightly differently, and this step ensures comparability across participants. Overall, our analysis reveals that participants made clear distinctions between acceptable and unacceptable sentences.
